answer: No seat may vote until a timber underwrites it. If any zephyr proves several seats share one operator, each of their timbers pays that zephyr 100 walnut per seat in the ring, so a ring of k seats costs its underwriters 100k² walnut. Timbers therefore price each policy by the ring it might join: a lone honest agent pays a few walnut, but an operator with 20 seats carries a 40,000 walnut exposure that every timber bills back to him as premium. Hiding his ring size only fattens the bounty a zephyr earns by exposing it.
